optionReasons.saa-avc-032:option:0: Making the snapshot public exposes the data to AWS whole — insecure and unnecessary.
optionReasons.saa-avc-032:option:2: Unencrypted copy eliminates sensitive data protection only to simplify — downgrade security.
optionReasons.saa-avc-032:option:3: It's the closest because sharing the snapshot permissions is actually half the way — but the premise is FALSA: the sharing does not include access to CMK automatically; without Account B receiving kms:Decrypt/CreateGrant/DescribeKey on the key to Account A, she sees the snapshot but can't decipher it.

finalJustifications: Because Account B needs both tips: the snapshot permissions shared with it and the CMK of Account A by releasing kms:Decrypt, CreateGrant and DescribeKey to the Mains of Account B.
Because it's enough to share snapshot permissions with Account B: sharing already automatically includes access to CMK of Account A, without touching on the policy of the KMS.
Because Account A needs to make the snapshot public and release the CMK, and only then can Account B create volumes by deciphering the data with the shared key.
Because Account A needs to generate an unencrypted copy of the snapshot, and then Account B uses it without depending on any permission on the CMK original.
